claim: Endosomes and lysosomes harbor Rab5 and Rab7 on their surface as key proteins involved in their identity, biogenesis, and fusion.
source: Endosomes and lysosomes harbor Rab5 and Rab7 on their surface as key proteins involved in their identity, biogenesis, and fusion.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about Rab proteins in the endolysosomal system.

claim: Mon1-Ccz1 is the guanine nucleotide exchange factor (GEF) for Rab7.
source: Rab activation requires a guanine nucleotide exchange factor (GEF), which is Mon1-Ccz1 for Rab7.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work by the authors and others.

claim: During endosome maturation, Rab5 is replaced by Rab7.
source: During endosome maturation, Rab5 is replaced by Rab7, though the underlying mechanism remains poorly understood.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, though the mechanism is noted as poorly understood.

claim: Mon1-Ccz1 is an effector of Rab5.
source: We show (i) that Mon1-Ccz1 is an effector of Rab5
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Membrane-bound Rab5 is the key factor to directly promote Mon1-Ccz1 dependent Rab7 activation and Rab7-dependent membrane fusion.
source: that membrane-bound Rab5 is the key factor to directly promote Mon1-Ccz1 dependent Rab7 activation and Rab7-dependent membrane fusion
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by in vitro reconstitution experiments shown in the figures.

claim: The Rab5 to Rab7 transition process is regulated in yeast by the casein kinase Yck3, which phosphorylates Mon1 and blocks Rab5 binding.
source: that this process is regulated in yeast by the casein kinase Yck3, which phosphorylates Mon1 and blocks Rab5 binding.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by phosphorylation and binding experiments shown in Figure 6.

claim: Endocytic vesicles carrying cargo molecules pinch off at the plasma membrane and fuse in a Rab5-dependent manner with early endosomes.
source: Endocytic vesicles carrying cargo molecules pinch off at the plasma membrane and fuse in a Rab5-dependent manner with early endosomes.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the endocytic pathway supported by citations.

claim: Early endosomes undergo fusion with other early endosomes, which in the end mature into late endosomes.
source: Early endosomes undergo fusion with other early endosomes, which in the end mature into late endosomes.
evidence: This is established knowledge about endosome maturation.

claim: Early endosomes and late endosomes carry Rab5 as an identity marker.
source: All these organelles carry Rab5 as an identity marker.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Rab5 localization.

claim: On the verge to late endosomes the identity changes from a Rab5-positive to a Rab7-positive compartment.
source: On the verge to late endosomes the identity changes from a Rab5-positive to a Rab7-positive compartment (Rink et al., 2005; Poteryaev et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The Rab5 to Rab7 transition allows fusion with the lysosome, where endocytic cargo is degraded.
source: This allows fusion with the lysosome, where endocytic cargo is degraded.
evidence: This is established knowledge about lysosomal function.

claim: Rab GTPases cycle between a GDP-bound (Rab-GDP) and a GTP-bound (Rab-GTP) state.
source: Rab GTPases cycle between a GDP-bound (Rab-GDP) and a GTP-bound (Rab-GTP) state (Hutagalung and Novick, 2011; Barr, 2013; Goody et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Rab GTPase function supported by citations.

claim: Rab-specific Guanine Nucleotide Exchange Factors (GEF) bind to the Rab GTPase and stabilize the nucleotide-free form to allow dissociation of bound nucleotide and binding of the more abundant GTP.
source: Rab-specific Guanine Nucleotide Exchange Factors (GEF) bind to the Rab GTPase and stabilize the nucleotide-free form to allow dissociation of bound nucleotide and binding of the more abundant GTP.
evidence: This is established knowledge about GEF function.

claim: GTPase-Activating Proteins (GAP) are needed to complete the active site of Rab GTPases to hydrolyze bound GTP to GDP.
source: GTPase-Activating Proteins (GAP) are needed to complete the active site of Rab GTPases to hydrolyze bound GTP to GDP.
evidence: This is established knowledge about GAP function.

claim: Only when bound to GTP the Rab GTPase can interact with specific effector proteins.
source: Only when bound to GTP the Rab GTPase can interact with specific effector proteins.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Rab GTPase regulation.

claim: Rab GTPases are C-terminally prenylated and can thus bind membranes.
source: Rab GTPases are C-terminally prenylated and can thus bind membranes (Goody et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Rab GTPases are kept soluble in the cytosol by binding in their GDP-form to the Rab Escort Protein (REP) in the context of their posttranslational prenylation or to the Guanine Nucleotide Dissociation Inhibitor (GDI) as their general Rab chaperone.
source: They are kept soluble in the cytosol by binding in their GDP-form to the Rab Escort Protein (REP) in the context of their posttranslational prenylation or to the Guanine Nucleotide Dissociation Inhibitor (GDI) as their general Rab chaperone.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Rab chaperone proteins.

claim: Rab5 marks early endosomes, whereas Rab7 is found on late endosomes, autophagosomes, and lysosomes.
source: Within the endolysosomal system, Rab5 marks early endosomes, whereas Rab7 is found on late endosomes, autophagosomes, and lysosomes (Chavrier et al., 1990; Bucci et al., 1992; Wichmann et al., 1992; Horazdovsky et al., 1994; Gutierrez et al., 2004; McEwan et al., 2015; Hegedűs et al., 2016; Gao et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: The Rab5 family has four members in human cells (Rab5a, 5b, 5c, 5d), one member in Drosophila melanogaster (RAB5), and at least three members in S. cerevisiae (Vps21, Ypt52, Ypt53).
source: The Rab5 family has four members in human cells (Rab5a, 5b, 5c, 5d), one member in Drosophila melanogaster (RAB5), and at least three members in S. cerevisiae (Vps21, Ypt52, Ypt53).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Rab5 family members across species.

claim: In human cells, Rab5 is activated by its GEF Rabex-5 in complex with the Rab5 effector Rabaptin5, which function together in a positive feedback loop to form a Rab5-domain on endosomes.
source: In human cells, Rab5 is activated by its GEF Rabex-5 in complex with the Rab5 effector Rabaptin5, which function together in a positive feedback loop to form a Rab5-domain on endosomes (Wandinger-Ness and Zerial, 2014; Franke et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: In yeast, at least three Rab5-GEFs have been identified.
source: In yeast, at least three Rab5-GEFs have been identified, which may function similarly (Burd et al., 1996; Paulsel et al., 2013; Cabrera et al., 2013; Bean et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The Mon1-Ccz1 complex was identified as the Rab7 GEF.
source: We and others identified the Mon1-Ccz1 complex as the Rab7 GEF (Nordmann et al., 2010; Gerondopoulos et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies by the authors and others.

claim: In yeast, Mon1-Ccz1 forms a dimer.
source: In yeast, Mon1-Ccz1 forms a dimer, whereas metazoan cells have a third subunit, named RMC1 in mammals (Vaites et al., 2018), and Bulli in Drosophila melanogaster (Dehnen et al., submitted).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: Metazoan cells have a third subunit in the Mon1-Ccz1 complex, named RMC1 in mammals and Bulli in Drosophila melanogaster.
source: In yeast, Mon1-Ccz1 forms a dimer, whereas metazoan cells have a third subunit, named RMC1 in mammals (Vaites et al., 2018), and Bulli in Drosophila melanogaster (Dehnen et al., submitted).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: Mon1-Ccz1 interactions with Rab5 have been shown by yeast-two- and three-hybrid studies and in pulldown experiments from lysates.
source: According to prevailing models, Mon1-Ccz1 is an effector of Rab5, and interactions have been shown by yeast-two- and three-hybrid studies and in pulldown experiments from lysates (Kinchen and Ravichandran, 2010; Cui et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Mon1-Ccz1 interacts with phosphatidylinositol-3-phosphate, PI-3-P.
source: Furthermore, Mon1-Ccz1 also interacts with phosphatidylinositol-3-phosphate, PI-3-P (Cabrera et al., 2014; Lawrence et al., 2014; Hegedűs et al., 2016), which is present on endosomes and autophagosomes (Schu et al., 1993; Kihara et al., 2001), and functions on endosomes (Yasuda et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: PI-3-P is present on endosomes and autophagosomes.
source: Furthermore, Mon1-Ccz1 also interacts with phosphatidylinositol-3-phosphate, PI-3-P (Cabrera et al., 2014; Lawrence et al., 2014; Hegedűs et al., 2016), which is present on endosomes and autophagosomes (Schu et al., 1993; Kihara et al., 2001), and functions on endosomes (Yasuda et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: Mon1/Sand1 alone can displace the Rab5 GEF Rabex-5 from membranes, thus promoting Rab5 release.
source: Moreover, it was shown that Mon1/Sand1 alone can displace the Rab5 GEF Rabex-5 from membranes, thus promoting Rab5 release (Poteryaev et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: A similar cascade of a Rab5 to Rab7 transition has been observed on mitochondria in vivo during Parkin-induced mitophagy.
source: A similar cascade of a Rab5 to Rab7 transition has been observed on mitochondria in vivo during Parkin-induced mitophagy (Yamano et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Mon1-Ccz1 inactivation impaired Rab7 recruitment during mitophagy.
source: Also here, Mon1-Ccz1 inactivation impaired Rab7 recruitment.
evidence: This is inferred from the previous sentence about mitophagy studies.

claim: Mon1-Ccz1 binds the LC3-like Atg8 protein and can thus recruit Ypt7 to the yeast autophagosomal membrane.
source: Finally, Mon1-Ccz1 binds the LC3-like Atg8 protein and can thus recruit Ypt7 to the yeast autophagosomal membrane (Gao et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Wild-type yeast cells take up FM4-64 readily, which results in staining of large vacuoles.
source: Wild-type cells take up FM4-64 readily, which results in staining of large vacuoles (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A,B.

claim: In mutants lacking mon1 less than 10% of the cells showed a normal vacuolar morphology.
source: In contrast, in mutants lacking mon1 less than 10% of the cells showed a normal vacuolar morphology.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Cells deleted for the endosomal Vps30 subunit of the PI-3-Kinase complex II had wild-type like vacuoles.
source: Cells deleted for the endosomal Vps30 subunit of the PI-3-Kinase complex II (Kihara et al., 2001), or two members of the Rab5-family, Vps21 and Ypt52, which upon deletion impair CORVET or retromer targeting (Cabrera et al., 2013; Paulsel et al., 2013), had wild-type like vacuoles.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A,B and citations.

claim: Cells deleted for two members of the Rab5-family, Vps21 and Ypt52, had wild-type like vacuoles.
source: Cells deleted for the endosomal Vps30 subunit of the PI-3-Kinase complex II (Kihara et al., 2001), or two members of the Rab5-family, Vps21 and Ypt52, which upon deletion impair CORVET or retromer targeting (Cabrera et al., 2013; Paulsel et al., 2013), had wild-type like vacuoles.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A,B and citations.

claim: Deletion of Vps21 and Ypt52 impair CORVET or retromer targeting.
source: Cells deleted for the endosomal Vps30 subunit of the PI-3-Kinase complex II (Kihara et al., 2001), or two members of the Rab5-family, Vps21 and Ypt52, which upon deletion impair CORVET or retromer targeting (Cabrera et al., 2013; Paulsel et al., 2013), had wild-type like vacuoles.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Combinations of different knockouts of members of the Rab5-family did not impair overall vacuole morphology.
source: Similarly, combinations of different knockouts of members of the Rab5-family did not impair overall vacuole morphology (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Deleting Vps30, Vps21 and Ypt52 together interfered with a normal endolysosomal maturation and fusion process and resulted in fragmented vacuoles as observed in mon1∆ cells.
source: However, deleting Vps30, Vps21 and Ypt52 together interfered with a normal endolysosomal maturation and fusion process and resulted in fragmented vacuoles as observed in mon1∆ cells (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Mon1-Ccz1 showed weak interactions with most of the tested Rab-GTPases including Vps21, Ypt52, or Ypt53.
source: Surprisingly, we only detected weak interactions with most of the tested Rab-GTPases (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), including either one of the well-studied Rab5-family members Vps21, Ypt52, or Ypt53.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Mon1-Ccz1 showed a strong interaction with Ypt10-GTP.
source: However, we observed a strong interaction with Ypt10-GTP (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Ypt10 has been assigned to the Rab5-family previously.
source: This poorly characterized Rab-GTPase has been assigned to the Rab5-family previously (Buvelot Frei et al., 2006; Lo et al., 2011), and localizes to FM4-64 positive structures in yeast
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Ypt10 localizes to FM4-64 positive structures in yeast.
source: This poorly characterized Rab-GTPase has been assigned to the Rab5-family previously (Buvelot Frei et al., 2006; Lo et al., 2011), and localizes to FM4-64 positive structures in yeast
evidence: This is inferred from the context and supported by citations.

claim: Ypt10 overexpression interferes with the endolysosomal system.
source: Ypt10 overexpression interferes with the endolysosomal system (Louvet et al., 1999), suggesting that the protein functions as a Rab5 protein under special growth conditions as shown for Ypt53 (Paulsel et al., 2013; Schmidt et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The endogenously expressed GFP-tagged Ypt10 and Ccz1-mCherry colocalized in dot-like structures proximal to the vacuole.
source: Indeed, the endogenously expressed GFP-tagged Ypt10 and Ccz1-mCherry colocalized in dot-like structures proximal to the vacuole (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: None of the single Rab5 deletions showed altered Ypt7 localization.
source: Interestingly, none of the single Rab5 deletions showed altered Ypt7 localization.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Deletion of both Vps21 and Ypt52 resulted in a dot-like localization of Ypt7, whereas FM4-64 still stained round vacuoles.
source: However, deletion of both Vps21 and Ypt52 resulted in a dot-like localization of Ypt7, whereas FM4-64 still stained round vacuoles (Figure 1A,F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A,F.

claim: Rab5-proteins can affect Ypt7 localization in vivo.
source: This suggests that Rab5-proteins can affect Ypt7 localization in vivo.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data on Ypt7 localization in Rab5 deletion strains.

claim: Using a neutral lipid mix, 21% of Mon1-Ccz1 was associated with the membrane fraction.
source: Using a neutral lipid mix, 21% of Mon1-Ccz1 was associated with the membrane fraction, which increased to 34% in the presence of PI-3-P and PI-3,5-P2.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Mon1-Ccz1 membrane association increased to 34% in the presence of PI-3-P and PI-3,5-P2.
source: Using a neutral lipid mix, 21% of Mon1-Ccz1 was associated with the membrane fraction, which increased to 34% in the presence of PI-3-P and PI-3,5-P2.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: When prenylated Vps21 was included, the membrane association of Mon1-Ccz1 increased to 46%.
source: When prenylated Vps21 was included, the membrane association of Mon1-Ccz1 increased further (46%, Figure 2B), comparable with Mon1-Ccz1 membrane association in the presence of prenylated Ypt10 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Mon1-Ccz1 takes advantage of a dual targeting mechanism to bind membranes via lipids and Rab5.
source: This suggests that Mon1-Ccz1 takes advantage of a dual targeting mechanism to bind membranes via lipids and Rab5.
evidence: This is inferred from the membrane binding data showing synergistic effects of lipids and Rab5.

claim: Mon1-Ccz1 showed comparable binding to membranes carrying other charged lipids at concentrations adjusted for equimolar negative charge.
source: We also observed comparable binding to membranes carrying other charged lipids at concentrations adjusted for equimolar negative charge (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Mon1-Ccz1 interacts with phospholipids via unspecific electrostatic interactions rather than specific lipid head group recognition.
source: Thus, Mon1-Ccz1 seems to interact with phospholipids via unspecific electrostatic interactions rather than specific lipid head group recognition.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing comparable binding to different charged lipids.

claim: Mon1-Ccz1 did not show any GEF activity using liposomes composed of a vacuolar mimicking lipid mix in the absence of a recruiter.
source: Surprisingly, we did not observe any GEF activity using liposomes composed of a vacuolar mimicking lipid mix (VML-liposomes) (Figure 3B, no recruiter), indicating that recruitment of Mon1-Ccz1 to membranes via charged lipids is not sufficient for GEF activity.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Recruitment of Mon1-Ccz1 to membranes via charged lipids is not sufficient for GEF activity.
source: Surprisingly, we did not observe any GEF activity using liposomes composed of a vacuolar mimicking lipid mix (VML-liposomes) (Figure 3B, no recruiter), indicating that recruitment of Mon1-Ccz1 to membranes via charged lipids is not sufficient for GEF activity.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing no GEF activity without a recruiter.

claim: Mon1-Ccz1 efficiently triggered nucleotide exchange of Ypt7 in the presence of the Rab5-like protein Vps21, but not the Golgi-Rab Ypt31.
source: When we now added pYpt7:GDI, Mon1-Ccz1 efficiently triggered nucleotide exchange of Ypt7 in the presence of the Rab5-like protein Vps21, but not the Golgi-Rab Ypt31 (Figure 3B,D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B,D.

claim: Even more GEF activity was observed when the Rab5-homologs Ypt52 or Ypt53 were present on membranes.
source: Even more activity was observed, when the Rab5-homologs Ypt52 or Ypt53 were present on membranes, and prenylated Ypt10 resulted in strongest GEF activity (Figure 3B,D)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B,D.

claim: Prenylated Ypt10 resulted in strongest GEF activity.
source: Even more activity was observed, when the Rab5-homologs Ypt52 or Ypt53 were present on membranes, and prenylated Ypt10 resulted in strongest GEF activity (Figure 3B,D)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B,D.

claim: Addition of soluble Ypt10 did not result in Mon1-Ccz1 activation.
source: whereas addition of soluble Ypt10 did not result in Mon-Ccz1 activation (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: There was no difference detected between Vps21, Ypt31, and Ypt10 amounts on membranes after the measurements.
source: To ask if the difference in activity is due to the amount of recruiter GTPase on membranes, we recovered membranes after the measurements, and did not detect any difference between Vps21, Ypt31, and Ypt10 amounts on membranes (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Mon1-Ccz1 dependent activation of the Rab7-like Ypt7 is strongly stimulated by Rab5-GTP on membranes and correlates with the affinity of the effector interaction between Rab and Mon1-Ccz1.
source: These data show that Mon1-Ccz1 dependent activation of the Rab7-like Ypt7 is strongly stimulated by Rab5-GTP on membranes and correlates with the affinity of the effector interaction between Rab and Mon1-Ccz1.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing differential GEF activity with different Rab5 proteins.

claim: No difference was observed in GEF activity for Drosophila Rab7-GEF in the absence or presence of the third subunit, named Bulli/CG8270, in solution.
source: We recently observed no difference in GEF activity for Drosophila Rab7-GEF in the absence or presence of the third subunit, named Bulli/CG8270 (Dehnen et al., submitted) in solution.
evidence: This is supported by citation to a submitted manuscript.

claim: Using either dimeric or trimeric Drosophila Mon1-Ccz1 complex, efficient GEF-activity was observed on VML-liposomes in the presence of DmpRab5.
source: Using either complex, we observed efficient GEF-activity on VML-liposomes in the presence of DmpRab5 (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: GEF-activity of the trimeric GEF was roughly comparable to the dimeric GEF.
source: GEF-activity of the trimeric GEF was roughly comparable to the dimeric GEF (Figure 4D,E), in agreement with their activity in solution using non-prenylated Rabs (Dehnen et al., submitted).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D,E and citation.

claim: No difference was observed in the membrane association of the recruiter between dimeric and trimeric Drosophila complexes.
source: We did not observe a difference in the membrane association of the recruiter (Figure 4—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1I.

claim: No GEF-activity of either dimeric or trimeric Drosophila complex was detected in the absence of a recruiter GTPase.
source: Notably, also in the Drosophila system, we did not detect GEF-activity of either complex in the absence of a recruiter GTPase (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Lower concentrations of pRab5 in the recruiter assay resulted in the same activity of dimer and trimer as reflected by the similar rate constant.
source: However, lower concentrations of pRab5 in the recruiter assay resulted in the same activity of dimer and trimer as reflected by the similar rate constant (Figure 4F,G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F,G.

claim: The ability of Rab5-dependent activation requires just the Mon1-Ccz1 core components in metazoan and yeast.
source: These data show that the ability of Rab5-dependent activation requires just the Mon1-Ccz1 core components – in metazoan and yeast.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data comparing dimeric and trimeric complexes.

claim: There is no evidence that the third subunit in the metazoan complex has a direct influence on the catalytic activity of Mon1-Ccz1.
source: Moreover, we find no evidence that the third subunit in the metazoan complex has a direct influence on the catalytic activity of Mon1-Ccz1.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing no difference between dimeric and trimeric complexes.

claim: The interaction of Rab5 with Bulli/CG8270 is indirect and mediated via Mon1-Ccz1.
source: Our data suggest that the interaction of Rab5 with Bulli/CG8270 (Gillingham et al., 2014) is indirect and mediated via Mon1-Ccz1.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data and supported by citation.

claim: Fusion of yeast SNARE-decorated proteoliposomes requires just four soluble factors: a soluble SNARE (Vam7), Mon1-Ccz1, the Rab7-GTPase (pYpt7:GDI), and the HOPS tethering complex.
source: We showed before that fusion of yeast SNARE-decorated proteoliposomes requires just four soluble factors: a soluble SNARE (Vam7), Mon1-Ccz1, the Rab7-GTPase (pYpt7:GDI), and the HOPS tethering complex (Langemeyer et al., 2018b; Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Mon1-Ccz1 activity was limiting for Ypt7 recruitment and activation and thus HOPS function.
source: Mon1-Ccz1 activity was limiting for Ypt7 recruitment and activation and thus HOPS function (Langemeyer et al., 2018b).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Only minimal fusion was detected at 12.5 nM Mon1-Ccz1 in the absence of a recruiter.
source: First, we titrated Mon1-Ccz1 into the fusion reaction, and detected only minimal fusion at 12.5 nM (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: In the presence of the recruiter pYpt10, fusion strongly increased at 12.5 nM Mon1-Ccz1.
source: However, in the presence of the recruiter pYpt10, this fusion strongly increased (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Comparable amounts of Ccz1 were observed in the membrane fraction in the presence or absence of Ypt10.
source: When we tested the membrane fraction after fusion for the presence of Mon1-Ccz1, we observed comparable amounts of Ccz1 in the membrane fraction.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D,E.

claim: The Ypt7-effector Vps41 as a subunit of HOPS was strongly enriched on membranes in the presence of Ypt10.
source: In contrast, the Ypt7-effector Vps41 as a subunit of HOPS was strongly enriched on membranes in the presence of Ypt10 (Figure 5D,E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D,E.

claim: Mon1-Ccz1 associates with membranes independently of a recruiter GTPase.
source: This indicates that Mon1-Ccz1 associates with membranes independently of a recruiter GTPase.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing comparable Mon1-Ccz1 membrane association with or without recruiter.

claim: Only in the presence of a Rab5-recruiter, Mon1-Ccz1 can exert sufficient GEF-activity to drive Ypt7 activation, and thereby HOPS recruitment and fusion.
source: Importantly, only in the presence of a Rab5-recruiter, Mon1-Ccz1 can exert sufficient GEF-activity to drive Ypt7 activation, and therey HOPS recruitment and fusion.
evidence: This is inferred from the fusion data showing strong dependence on Rab5 recruiter.

claim: Rab5 directly stimulates catalytic activity of Mon1-Ccz1 beyond promoting binding to the membrane.
source: This suggests that Rab5 directly stimulates catalytic activity of Mon1-Ccz1 beyond promoting binding to the membrane.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing membrane binding without recruiter but no activity.

claim: Mon1 was identified as a target of the vacuolar type 1 casein kinase Yck3 in a previous study.
source: In a previous study, we identified Mon1 as a target of the vacuolar type 1 casein kinase Yck3 (Lawrence et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Phosphorylation of Mon1 results in an upshift on SDS gels and release of the protein from vacuoles during in vitro vacuole fusion.
source: Phosphorylation of Mon1 results in an upshift on SDS gels and release of the protein from vacuoles during in vitro vacuole fusion.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Yck3 has several targets at the vacuole, including the HOPS subunit Vps41 and the SNARE Vam3.
source: Yck3 has several targets at the vacuole, including the HOPS subunit Vps41 and the SNARE Vam3 (LaGrassa and Ungermann, 2005; Brett et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Successful phosphorylation of Mon1-Ccz1 by Yck3 was judged by an upshift of Mon1 on SDS gels.
source: Successful phosphorylation was judged by an upshift of Mon1 on SDS gels (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: A strong decrease in GEF-activity of the phosphorylated Mon1-Ccz1 complex was observed compared to the mock-treated complex.
source: Using pretreated Mon1-Ccz1, we observed a strong decrease in GEF-activity of the phosphorylated complex (complete) compared to the mock-treated complex, where either Yck3 (no Yck3) or ATP (no ATP) was omitted (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A,B.

claim: Yck3-mediated phosphorylation strongly inhibits Rab5-dependent Mon1-Ccz1 activation.
source: This shows that Yck3-mediated phosphorylation strongly inhibits Rab5-dependent Mon1-Ccz1 activation.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing decreased GEF activity after phosphorylation.

claim: Phosphorylated Mon1 was less efficiently recruited onto membranes than non-phosphorylated Mon1 in the presence of Vps21 or Ypt10.
source: We also analyzed Mon1 in the same membrane fractions. Phosphorylated Mon1 was less efficiently recruited onto membranes than non-phosphorylated Mon1 in the presence of Vps21 or Ypt10 (Figure 6C, lane 1 and 9).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Phosphorylated Mon1 also associated with membrane in the absence of the recruiter GTPase.
source: We noticed that phosphorylated Mon1 also associated with membrane in the absence of the recruiter GTPase (Figure 6C, lane 7 and 15) as observed for non-phosphorylated Mon1 in the fusion assay (Figure 5D), yet this association does not have any effect on GEF activity (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C, 5D, and 6A.

claim: In the absence of the kinase Yck3, Mon1-Ccz1 interacted robustly with Ypt10-GTP, and weakly with Vps21-GTP.
source: In the absence of the kinase Yck3, Mon1-Ccz1 interacted robustly with Ypt10-GTP, and weakly with Vps21-GTP as observed before (Figure 1D, Figure 6D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D and Figure 6D.

claim: The nucleotide specificity of Mon1-Ccz1 interaction with Rab5 proteins was completely lost after Yck3-mediated phosphorylation.

claim: Phosphorylation blocks the specific interaction with Rab5-proteins and could support Mon1-Ccz1 recycling from membranes.

claim: Mon1-Ccz1 has a dual membrane targeting mechanism by binding both Rab5 and charged lipids like PI-3-P.

source: Our data reveal that Mon1-Ccz1 is an evolutionarily conserved effector of Rab5, both in yeast and Drosophila.

claim: The PI-3-Kinase Vps34 is a Rab5 effector.

claim: Endosomal Rabs are not uniformly distributed along the endosomal membrane.

claim: Non-uniform distribution of Rabs could result in selective enrichment of Mon1-Ccz1 and thus Rab7 to distinct domains on endosomes.
